transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-07 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Roberto Singh (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Lara Kim (NovaSearch, ML Eng); Ethan Patel (NovaSearch, Platform); Sofia Ruiz (NovaSearch, CTO)
Links shared: 1) benchmark spreadsheet (drive) - Maya to share trimmed version; 2) security checklist (redwood.com/security) - Maya

Summary: quick check-in on quantization experiments (INT8 vs FP8). Reviewed initial perf deltas and quality impact on NovaSearch ranking / NLU tasks. Agreed next steps to run a 4k prompt eval, provision a VPC test environment for latency runs, and share detailed logs and cost estimates. Discussed security/compliance items (KMS, audit logs, retention) and tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Hosted for latency stability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Roberto from infra, Priya CSM, and then NovaSearch team?
[00:06] Lara: Hi yep Lara here.
[00:08] Ethan: Ethan on platform.
[00:10] Sofia: Sofia here.
[00:12] Maya: Great. Agenda is short — results from last week's INT8/FP8 runs, quality checks, and decide the next experiments. Roberto, do you want to lead?
[00:20] Roberto (Redwood SE): Sure. Quick note, we've been running two branches: one quantized to INT8 using the per-channel aware flow, and one FP8 sim (fp8-e4m3-ish) — these are on the same model variant you provided, the 7B re-ranked model. Results are preliminary.
[00:35] Lara: Quick clarifying question — the dataset you used was the 2k dev set we uploaded, right?
[00:39] Roberto: Correct, the 2k dev plus a 500 sample holdout for manual review. We saw consistent throughput improvements vs baseline.
[00:46] [00:46] Roberto: INT8: ~1.8x throughput, median p99 latency down by ~25-28% on the same GPU pool. FP8: ~1.4x throughput, p99 down ~12-15%.
[01:03] Ethan: Those are good numbers. What about quality? Any big regressions?
[01:08] Roberto: On automated metrics — accuracy on the rerank task dropped by ~0.7% absolute for INT8, FP8 dropped by ~0.3%. For NLU classification the F1 delta was small: INT8 -0.9, FP8 -0.4.
[01:23] Lara: Hmm okay, 0.7% sounds small but for our top-recall slice it might matter. Did you look at the tail cases?
[01:28] Roberto: Yes we sampled the top 200 worst-delta cases. Many are hallucination-like or long-context edge cases where quantization slightly alters token probabilities. Some proper nouns got noisy — e.g., 'Kahna' vs 'Khana' got confused in a few.
[01:45] Maya: That's consistent with our expectations — INT8 tends to be more aggressive and you'll see a few more tail issues. FP8 is a middle ground.
[01:53] Sofia: From a product lens, what matters is whether those tail cases affect real user metrics — CTR/relevance. Can we run an A/B small pilot with INT8 and monitor user impact?
[02:02] Maya: Yes, two options: Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity gives more stable latency for a rollout, or hosted with canary routing and fallback if we see regressions. Both are possible.
[02:12] Ethan: For privacy/reg compliance, we prefer VPC/private deployment for the POC. Is the Private path going to support the quantized runtimes?
[02:18] Roberto: Yes. Redwood Private supports the same runtime, quantization is supported on the on-prem or VPC deployment as long as the serving infra has the compatible kernels. We did see slight kernel variance between Ampere vs Hopper GPU builds — that affected fp8 perf a bit.
[02:33] Lara: Any gotchas re: KV cache or stateful chat? We have some conversation contexts that rely on long KV cache.
[02:38] Roberto: Good point — INT8 can affect KV cache memory layout slightly; in our tests the effective cache hit rate was the same but memory pressure went up marginally. We monitored KV cache hits and saw no functional loss, only tuning required for batch sizes.
[02:51] [02:51] Priya (CSM): There were a couple of infra flaps early in the run, not related to quantization — just FYI, Ethan, we saw one instance where the node restarted and the job failedover. Logs are in the sheet.
[03:03] Ethan: Got it we'll look. We need reproducible logs for legal/bench acceptance.
[03:08] Roberto: We preserved full raw logs; Maya will share a trimmed copy.
[03:12] Maya: I'll post the benchmark spreadsheet with the perf and raw logs link after this call.
[03:18] Lara: Back to quality — can you run a targeted eval on our high-value queries? We have a 400-sample 'top-slice' that drives most of our revenue.
[03:25] Roberto: Yes. We'll run both quantization modes on that slice and produce a confusion table and worst-case examples.
[03:31] Lara: Sounds great. Please surface examples where INT8 flips the top-1 ranking.
[03:36] Roberto: Will do.
[03:38] [03:38] Sofia: On security, last time we asked about KMS integration and audit logs. What's the status?
[03:44] Maya: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private and Dedicated. Audit logs and retention controls are standard — we can configure S3 retention or push to your SIEM. I'll attach the security checklist link.
[03:58] Ethan: For the VPC test we need SAML SSO and scoping for temporary access. Also need to know data retention defaults so legal can sign off.
[04:07] Priya: Noted; we'll get SAML docs and retention policy into the ticket.
[04:11] Lara: On cost — can you give a rough cost delta if we use INT8 in production vs baseline FP32?
[04:16] Roberto: Very rough ballpark from our runs: INT8 reduces token compute cost by ~40-45% at observed batching; FP8 ~25-30%. Actual billing depends on your batch sizes and sequence lengths. We'll run cost sim across your median seq length and send numbers.
[04:31] Ethan: Excellent. For the pilot we want cost + quality tradeoff chart.
[04:35] Maya: We'll deliver that.
[04:38] [04:38] Lara: Anything unexpected in the perf deltas?
[04:41] Roberto: One note — on Hopper GPUs FP8 performance is closer to INT8 for some ops; on older Ampere cards the INT8 advantage is clearer. So hardware profile matters. Also we found a minor tokenizer edge-case where byte-level rounding changed whitespace tokens leading to slight rank differences.
[04:58] Maya: Good callout. We'll annotate the spreadsheet with hardware columns.
[05:02] Sofia: For decision-making, what's the recommended path? Pilot with FP8 to reduce risk or INT8 to maximize savings?
[05:09] Roberto: I usually recommend FP8 for initial canary because it reduces cost but keeps closer to FP32 quality. If after the 4k eval we see acceptable delta, INT8 could be used for non-critical paths or with fallback to FP32 for low-confidence queries.
[05:24] Lara: Can Redwood runtime do dynamic fallback — like route a request to FP32 if model confidence is low?
[05:29] Roberto: Yes, we have routing policies: confidence thresholding + automatic fallback to a compatible variant. It's been used in other pilots. There is a small latency cost for fallback but it's manageable.
[05:40] Ethan: We'll need instrumentation — per-request cost & latency and token-level breakdown. Does Redwood Console show token-level traces?
[05:46] Maya: Yep token-level cost and latency breakdowns are in Redwood Console. We can create a project dashboard and share read-only access.
[05:52] [05:52] Priya: I'll set up the dashboard and invite the NovaSearch read-only group.
[05:56] Lara: Great. For the 4k prompt eval you mentioned, what exactly will you run?
[06:00] Roberto: We'll run both quant modes across your 4k sample set (combining dev+edge slices), collect automated metrics (accuracy, F1, nDCG depending on task), and extract top-100 worst deltas for manual review. We'll also capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, GPU util, and memory.
[06:16] Lara: Timeline?
[06:18] Roberto: I can kick that off once Ethan gives the VPC test access; estimate 48-72 hours to run and analyze, so by 2026-04-13-ish.
[06:27] Ethan: I'll aim to provision by 2026-04-12.
[06:30] Maya: We'll mirror logs to your S3 for traceability.
[06:33] [06:33] Sofia: A question about deployment: if we go Dedicated vs Private, how does rollback look? We want rapid rollback if user metrics show regression.
[06:41] Roberto: Both support canary rollouts with automatic rollback. Dedicated gives more predictable latency for steady traffic; Private gives you full network control. Rollback is a config change and typically takes seconds to route, depending on in-flight requests.
[06:55] Lara: Any legal / procurement blockers?
[06:58] Maya: We'll include standard terms; Priya will surface any custom data residency or retention terms in the ticket.
[07:05] Priya: Sending the initial contract template to Ethan after the call.
[07:09] Ethan: Thanks.
[07:11] [07:11] Lara: Can you also surface the concrete examples where FP8 performs better than INT8 (if any)?
[07:15] Roberto: In our runs FP8 had fewer hallucination flips in long-context passages — likely due to smoother dynamic range. We'll extract examples.
[07:23] Maya: Ok to recap and action items?
[07:26] Lara: Yep.
[07:27] Maya: Recap: 1) Roberto runs 4k prompt eval for INT8 and FP8 and posts results by 2026-04-13; 2) Ethan provisions VPC/test infra by 2026-04-12; 3) Maya shares trimmed benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs by 2026-04-09; 4) Priya sets up Redwood Console dashboard and invites NovaSearch group; 5) Follow-up sync scheduled for 2026-04-14 to review final numbers and discuss pilot A/B.
[07:54] Ethan: Sounds good.
[07:56] Sofia: Good meeting, thank you.
[07:58] Maya: Thanks everyone.
